name: De Forest three-electrode Audion
description: An early three-electrode electron tube with a grid between filament and plate, used as a radio detector.

date.basis: ETHW distinguishes the initial two-electrode device in 1906 and addition of the grid within a year.

events.statement: De Forest developed an Audion electron tube and added a third control electrode by about 1907.

evidence.supports: Smithsonian attributes the Audion to De Forest and dates its invention and patent.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated witness established by the cited source for this scoped record, not a claim of global first.

caveats: Early Audions varied; their later amplification and oscillator applications require separate event-specific evidence. Sources differ on exactly when the first three-electrode variant appeared.
